reuse.why: Reuses recurrence conversion and weekend helpers, but consumers assemble the occurrence-skipping policy separately.

duplication.why: The combined daily-skip and nonworking-day decision appears in getNextDate, both schedule handlers, and budget templates.

placement.why: Holiday classification and movement belong in shared/schedules.ts, but occurrence eligibility remains scattered into handlers and budget logic.

scope.why: Changes are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared holiday matching is straightforward, but separate eligibility filters and occurrence-search bounds create multiple places to maintain the same policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts requests raw dates through getNextDate(..., true) and implements eligibility locally; both app.ts handlers likewise assemble filtering outside the shared date-selection path.

disguised_duplication.where: The same occurrence-eligibility decision is reshaped as an isKept predicate in getNextDate, a continue condition in getDatesInRange, an array filter in getUpcomingDates, and a conditional accumulation in createScheduleList.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; daily-specific decisions enter skipsWeekendOccurrences, applyWeekendRule, and applyWeekendRuleToDay, while the two handlers and budget template retain local eligibility filtering.
